clue.text: 21 back in crowd — foolish behaviour

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed in the middle of the word for crowd

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people

indicators.note: back tells us to read the answer to 21 down from right to left

parts.note: the answer to 21 down, a word for finish

explanation.surface: Someone describes a mob behaving foolishly, apparently with some backstory.
explanation.walkthrough: The '21' is a cross-reference to the down clue's answer; 'back' turns it round and 'in' places it within the crowd word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy or folly in conduct is called madness, a direct synonym.

clue.text: US State girl is found with drink by private investigator

parts.note: miss is a title and word for a young unmarried woman
to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A girl is spotted drinking alongside a detective somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Mississippi is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: No teetotaller, the German crossing skating area

indicators.note: the German article stretches across, enclosing the skating area word

explanation.surface: A German who enjoys a drink skates across the ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' here means spanning: the German article goes either side of the rink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not a teetotaller takes alcohol, so is a drinker; the definition is a negative description.

clue.text: In sympathy with parent pro upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the two words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase describes being in harmony or close understanding with someone, so in sympathy.

clue.text: Use Crete as setting for mystery

indicators.note: the two clue words act as a setting that holds the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: An author is advised to set a mystery novel on the island of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret is something kept hidden from others, hence a mystery.

clue.text: District Attorney referring to challenge

parts.note: DA is the abbreviation for a US District Attorney
re is a word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A prosecutor brings up a legal challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to challenge them to do something bold; a noun synonym too.

clue.text: Reportedly completed in brownish-grey colour

parts.note: done means finished or completed

explanation.definitionFit: Dun is the name for a dull greyish-brown, as of a horse's coat.

clue.text: Provoke complaint — starter missing

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble or complaint

explanation.walkthrough: 'starter missing' looks like food; it drops the G from GROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir or provoke them into action or feeling.

clue.text: Winter sportsman or cricketer hitting high ball

definitions.meaning: one who glides down snowy slopes on skis
in cricket a hit sent steeply up into the air is called by this name

explanation.surface: Two sporting pictures: a winter athlete and a batsman lofting the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'skier' is a ball hit very high, usually an easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person on skis and, in cricket, a ball hit high into the air.

clue.text: After first sign of crime, make certain there's condemnation

indicators.note: after places the word for make certain behind the single letter
the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: Once a crime is spotted, people make sure the wrongdoer is condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is strong official disapproval or criticism, a synonym of condemnation.

clue.text: Unusually courteous, getting article for one — draw conclusions!

parts.note: extra can mean unusually, as in extra large

indicators.note: the article stands in for the letter meaning one, swapping one letter in the phrase

I is the Roman numeral for one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a very polite person reaching conclusions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' looks like an anagram signal but means EXTRA; in POLITE the I is swapped for A.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to infer or project conclusions from known facts, so draw conclusions.

clue.text: Sort of dislike oddly ignored

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A sort of mild aversion, oddly overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or type, as in people of that ilk, a synonym of sort.

clue.text: Gift I'd kept inside for top politician

clue.text: Expands popular features of cricket pitch

creases are the white lines marked on a cricket pitch for the batsman and bowler

clue.text: Tree initially as charming as collection in arboretum

clue.text: Sound of satisfaction turning over in bed not to be trusted

clue.text: Manoeuvred canoe in water

clue.text: Finish the season tired ultimately
